title: Maximum Side Length of a Square with Sum Less than or Equal to Threshold
summary: Determine the largest square submatrix within a given m x n matrix whose sum of elements is less than or equal to a specified threshold, or return 0 if no such square exists.
statement: Determine the largest square submatrix within a given m x n matrix whose sum of elements is less than or equal to a specified threshold, or return 0 if no such square exists.
constraints: mat is a nonempty rectangular matrix of nonnegative integers.
A candidate must be a contiguous square whose total is at most threshold.
Return its maximum side length, or zero when even every one-cell square is too large.
hints: Use four prefix values to test any square sum in constant time.
Because entries are nonnegative, binary-search the largest side having at least one valid square.
If a side works, every smaller side inside it works; this monotonicity makes binary search valid.
editorial: A padded 2D prefix table answers every square sum with inclusion-exclusion. Nonnegative cells guarantee that a valid square contains a valid square of every smaller side, so existence is monotone by side length. Binary search that predicate. The oracle directly sums every cell of every candidate square.

tests.explanation: A two-by-two block of ones totals four; no larger square fits.
Every one-cell square exceeds one, so the answer is zero.
